name: Oral Comprehension
definition: The ability to listen to and understand information and ideas presented through spoken words and sentences.

benchmark.name: Spoken-SQuAD
benchmark.model_or_system: ALBERT-large (fine-tuned on Text-SQuAD, evaluated on ASR transcripts of the Spoken-SQuAD test set)
benchmark.metric: F1 (%) on the Spoken-SQuAD test set
benchmark.human_reference: General adult / educated workforce listening to spoken expository passages (Wikipedia-style) and answering factual questions about them

benchmark.name: Spoken SQuAD
benchmark.model_or_system: You et al. 2021: BERT-based SQA model with self-supervised auxiliary tasks, contrastive learning and Temporal-Alignment Attention
benchmark.metric: F1 (%) on the Spoken SQuAD test set
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce: literate adults who listen to spoken informational content such as briefings, lectures and explanations at work and answer factual questions about it.

benchmark.name: SLURP
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population: typical people who listen to and act on short spoken requests at work, such as assistants and customer service staff.

benchmark.name: MMAU
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on the MMAU test split, overall average across sound, music and speech domains, multiple-choice
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated adult workforce: typical attentive adult listeners, comparable to the human evaluators used in the MMAU paper.

benchmark.name: MMSU
benchmark.human_reference: General educated adult workforce who listen to and interpret speech at work (native-level listeners without specialist phonetics training)

benchmark.name: MMSU
benchmark.human_reference: General adult / educated workforce listeners who understand spoken information in work settings. The MMSU human baseline of 89.72% is used as the proxy for the median relevant human.
